---
title: "MBCO on medfit SEM Models"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(RMediation)
# The chunks that fit models need medfit 0.9.0 or later, which is not on CRAN yet. Without it the code is
# shown and not run, and the text states what it returns.
have_medfit <- requireNamespace("medfit", quietly = TRUE) &&
  utils::packageVersion("medfit") >= "0.9.0"
```

`mbco()` can test a constraint on two models fitted with medfit's own SEM engine (`SEMFit` objects) instead of OpenMx. It compares the two fits with a chi-squared difference test, refits nothing, and needs no OpenMx. This page shows the route end to end and lists exactly what it refuses. For the OpenMx route, the bootstrap types and the product null, see [Testing an Indirect Effect with MBCO](mbco.html).

## 1. Fit the pair

Fit the full model (`h1`) and the same model with the constraint added (`h0`). The restricted model goes first in the `mbco()` call. Here the null is that the product of two paths is zero, `a1*b1 == 0`, in the `memory_exp` data that ships with the package:

```{r fit, eval = have_medfit}
d <- as.data.frame(memory_exp)
d$x <- as.numeric(d$x) - 1
syntax <- paste(
  "repetition ~ a1*x",
  "imagery ~ a2*x",
  "recall ~ cp*x + b1*repetition + b2*imagery",
  sep = "\n"
)
full <- medfit::fit_sem(syntax, d, fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = NULL)
null <- medfit::fit_sem(
  paste(syntax, "a1*b1 == 0", sep = "\n"), d,
  fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = NULL
)
```

Pass `fixed_x` and `meanstructure` yourself. medfit changed their defaults in 0.15.0 and warns before that, so a call that leaves them out can change meaning when medfit updates; the values above are the ones the package's own tests use.

## 2. Test and read the result

```{r mbco, eval = have_medfit}
res <- mbco(null, full)
res
```

With these data the statistic is 0.0831 on 1 degree of freedom, `p = 0.7731`. The test type is always `"asymp"` here, so the test uses no random numbers and there is no seed to report. The result is an ordinary `MBCOResult`: `res@statistic`, `res@df` and `res@p_value` hold the numbers. Its `@provenance` records the RMediation, medfit and R versions, which is what to cite; see [Reporting RMediation in a Paper](reporting.html).

## 3. What it refuses

Each of these stops with a message, so a mistake is loud:

| You do | You get |
|---|---|
| put the full model first | `h0 must have more degrees of freedom than h1: supply the restricted SEMFit first.` |
| ask for a bootstrap (`type = "semi"` or `"parametric"`) | `Assertion on 'type' failed: Must be element of set {'asymp'}` |
| pass OpenMx controls or any extra argument (`R = 10`) | `unused arguments for SEMFit: OpenMx fitting controls and other dots are not supported.` |
| mix a `SEMFit` with an OpenMx model | `mbco() requires two SEMFit objects or two OpenMx models; mixed pairs are not supported.` |
| use medfit older than 0.8.0 | `mbco() for SEMFit requires medfit >= 0.8.0` |
| test a null that sits on the boundary of the parameter space | `mbco() cannot report a chi-square p-value for a SEMFit null on the boundary`, with medfit's own explanation appended |

The last row matters most for variance constraints: when the tested value is a bound, an ordinary chi-squared p-value is not valid, medfit says so in a warning, and `mbco()` turns that warning into an error instead of returning a number.

## 4. What stays your responsibility

`mbco()` compares the two fits and checks only what the table above lists. It does not check that `h0` is nested in `h1` in substance, and it does not choose a reference distribution: the p-value is the asymptotic chi-squared one. A null such as `a1*b1 == 0` is a nonlinear constraint, so decide whether that reference is justified before you report the p-value. The OpenMx route has a dedicated test for this null, `mbco_product_null()`, described in [Testing an Indirect Effect with MBCO](mbco.html). The SEMFit route is described in [Status and Roadmap](roadmap.html); the CRAN question is on hold until a medfit release with the features it needs is on CRAN.
